name: Distroless
summary: A family of minimal OCI base images and Bazel build definitions supplying selected runtime dependencies for application images. Standard variants omit package managers and shells; separate debug variants add diagnostic tooling.

features.name: Minimal runtime content
features.description: Standard Distroless base images supply selected runtime dependencies while omitting package managers and shells. Consumers add their application artifacts; debug variants deliberately include additional tools.
benefits: Reduces runtime image contents and potential scanner noise
Narrows the software provenance surface of a deployed image
costs: Interactive debugging and package installation are unavailable by default
Applications must supply compatible entrypoints and dependencies

features.name: Bazel OCI image construction
features.description: The repository builds image variants with Bazel rules that assemble filesystem archives, package inputs, OCI images, and multi-architecture image indexes.
benefits: Makes image construction declarative and inspectable
Generates related runtime and debug variants from shared definitions
costs: Bazel rules and upstream package inputs become build dependencies
The build graph adds tooling and configuration complexity; a source commit alone does not identify a deployed image digest

features.name: Nonroot and debug variants
features.description: Distroless build definitions produce root and nonroot image variants and separate debug variants, allowing a smaller production-oriented image and a diagnostic image to share base construction logic.
benefits: Separates diagnostic tooling from the minimal runtime image
costs: Variant selection must match deployment and debugging workflows
Debug images do not represent the exact production artifact

mathematical_views.question: What minimal set of application and runtime files is sufficient to execute a workload in a Distroless image?
assumptions: The application dependency closure is known
The host supplies the container execution boundary
Absence of a shell is treated as a deliberate image property

mathematical_views.question: How do package inputs, architecture-specific layers, variants, and OCI indexes compose into published images?
assumptions: OCI indexes select compatible architecture images
The model abstracts registry publication and signature verification

costs: Bazel and package graph complexity; reproducibility requires fixed inputs
